h1: The 7 Best TVs Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best TVs under $200, from 50 inch 4K Fire TVs to 40 inch Roku and QLED sets, compared on size, resolution, and platform.
summary: The INSIGNIA 50 inch F50 Series is our top pick, offering 4K and Fire TV at a $100 to $200 price. The TOSHIBA 50 inch C350 is the close alternative, while the Hisense 40 inch QLED is the one for better color in a smaller size. The INSIGNIA F40 is the lowest-cost option, and the Roku Select suits anyone who prefers Roku.
intro: Under $200 the real decision is size versus resolution. A 50 inch 4K set and a 40 inch 1080p set cost about the same, and which is better depends on how far you sit from the screen and what room it goes in.

We reviewed seven TVs on paper, comparing screen size, resolution, smart platform, and display technology. The spec sheets here are thin, so the ranking leans on size, resolution, and platform rather than picture-quality claims we cannot verify.

products.name: INSIGNIA 50" Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: A 50 inch 4K Fire TV in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA F50 is a 50 inch LED television with 4K UHD resolution and the Fire TV smart platform. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It leads because it offers the most screen and the highest resolution here for a similar price. The TOSHIBA matches the size and resolution, but the INSIGNIA ranks first on balance.

Buy it for a living room or bedroom where you sit at a normal viewing distance. The caveat is that the listing data does not detail HDR or panel type.
products.idealFor: Living rooms and bedrooms wanting a big 4K screen.
products.skipIf: Your room is small or wall space is limited.

products.name: TOSHIBA 50" Class C350 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: Same size and resolution as the INSIGNIA, from another brand.
products.description:
The TOSHIBA C350 is a 50 inch 4K UHD LED set with Fire TV, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It matches the INSIGNIA on the three specs that matter most, so the choice is a coin flip on paper. We place it second because the INSIGNIA family also has more variants for matching sizes later.

Buy it if you find it cheaper than the INSIGNIA. The caveat is that the spec data is equally thin.
products.idealFor: Shoppers who want the same size at the better price.

products.name: Hisense 40-Inch Class QD4SR Series Hi-QLED FHD Smart Roku TV (40QD4SR
products.verdict: QLED color tech in a 40 inch Roku set.
products.description:
The Hisense QD4SR is a 40 inch Hi-QLED television at full HD resolution, running the Roku smart platform. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

QLED refers to a quantum dot layer meant to widen the color range, which is the reason it beats the other 40 inch sets on paper. It does give up the resolution of the 50 inch 4K models.

Buy it for a bedroom or desk setup. The caveat is 1080p at 40 inches.

products.name: Hisense 40-Inch Class A4 Series FHD 1080p Smart Fire TV (40A4NF) -
products.verdict: A 40 inch full HD Fire TV from Hisense.
products.description:
The Hisense A4 is a 40 inch full HD 1080p set with Fire TV, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It places behind the QD4SR since that model adds QLED for the same size, but it appeals to anyone who prefers the Fire TV interface over Roku.

Buy it for a small room if you like Fire TV. The caveat is a plain 1080p panel.
products.idealFor: Small rooms with a Fire TV preference.

products.name: INSIGNIA 40" Class FE Series LED Full HD Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: A 40 inch Fire TV with Alexa built in.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA FE is a 40 inch LED full HD television with Fire TV and Alexa, priced at $100 to $200.

The Alexa feature is what separates it from the plain F40 below, adding voice control, though it costs more. It does not match the Hisense A4's brand weight.

Buy it if you like voice control. The caveat is that the F40 is cheaper for the same size.

products.name: Roku 40-Inch Select Series Smart TV 2026-1080p Full HD TV - RokuTV
products.description:
The Roku Select Series is a 40 inch full HD television made by Roku, running RokuTV, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Being made by the platform's own maker is the pitch. On paper it offers the same 40 inch 1080p as rivals, with no display technology edge.

Buy it for simple Roku use. The caveat is that nothing here beats the Hisense QD4SR on specs.
products.idealFor: Roku users who want a simple set.

products.name: INSIGNIA 40" Class F40 Series LED Full HD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: The cheapest set here, at $50 to $100.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA F40 is a 40 inch full HD LED television with Fire TV, and it is the only one in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It ranks last for features, but its price is half that of most others, which makes it ideal as a second TV. The FE version adds Alexa.

Buy it for a kitchen, guest room, or dorm. The caveat is that it offers no extras.
products.skipIf: This is your main living room TV.

whatMatters.detail: A bigger screen needs more viewing distance. A 50 inch set suits sitting about six to eight feet away, and 40 inch suits closer. Measure your seating distance.
4K has four times the pixels of 1080p. At 40 inches the difference is small, but at 50 it is clearer. Check the resolution in the title.
Both stream the major services. Fire TV integrates with Alexa and Roku has a simple home screen. Pick the one you already use.
QLED uses quantum dots to widen color. It is a display technology label, not a guarantee of picture quality. Check the title.
Budget TV listings often omit HDR, panel type, and ports. Check the product page for HDMI count and refresh rate.

faq.q: Will a 4K TV look better than 1080p?
faq.a: At 50 inches yes, at 40 inches less so.

faq.q: Is the INSIGNIA worth it over the TOSHIBA?
faq.a: On paper they match. Buy whichever is cheaper.

faq.q: How do I set up a smart TV?
faq.a: Connect to Wi-Fi, sign in to your account, and download your apps.
Check the VESA pattern on the listing and buy a matching bracket.
Budget TV speakers are basic, so a soundbar helps if you care about audio.

finalTake: The INSIGNIA 50 inch F50 is the best buy under $200 for most living rooms, with 4K and Fire TV. Choose the Hisense QD4SR for a bedroom with better color, or the INSIGNIA F40 for a cheap second TV. Check the live price and confirm HDMI ports on the product page.
